speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To help me understand the severity and cause of your symptoms, please describe the appearance and location of your skin lesions. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), and C-Reactive Protein (CRP).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. ERYTHROCYTE SEDIMENTATION RATE (ESR): NORMAL READINGS. C-REACTIVE PROTEIN (CRP): NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the elevated white blood cell count with normal inflammatory markers is a significant clue. Could you tell me how many skin lesions you have and whether they are itchy or painful? Also, do you have a history of recent travel or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (GC).

The combination of recent sexually active behavior, a history of self-resolving migratory arthralgia (knee pain), and the current presentation of fever, chills, and monoarthritis in the wrist is highly characteristic of Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. The normal inflammatory markers despite leukocytosis also align with the pauci-inflammatory nature of this condition.
